subject: ela
intro: Authors write informational text to share ideas and convince readers. To support a point, authors give REASONS. A reason explains WHY something is true. Students learn to ask: 'What does the author want me to believe?' and 'What reason does the author give to support that?' This skill builds critical reading and helps students evaluate whether reasons are connected to the author's point.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

'Dogs make wonderful pets. They are loyal and always happy to see you when you come home. Dogs also love to play and can make you feel less lonely.'

What point does the author make? What reason does the author give to support it?

steps: First I ask: what does the author want me to believe? Dogs make wonderful pets.
Then I ask: what reason does the author give? That dogs are loyal and happy to see you.
A second reason is that dogs love to play and can make you feel less lonely.
Both reasons explain WHY dogs make good pets.
solution.answer: The author's point is that dogs make wonderful pets. The reasons given are: (1) dogs are loyal and happy to see you, and (2) they love to play and can make you feel less lonely.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

'You should drink water every day. Water helps your body work. It keeps your brain thinking clearly and gives your muscles energy.'

What is the author's point? What reasons support it?

steps: Ask: what does the author want me to believe? I should drink water every day.
Ask: what reasons does the author give? Water helps your body work.
More specific reasons: it keeps your brain thinking clearly and gives your muscles energy.
These are two reasons that explain why drinking water is important.
solution.answer: The author's point is that you should drink water every day. The reasons are: (1) water helps your body work, (2) it keeps your brain thinking clearly, and (3) it gives your muscles energy.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

'Libraries are great places for children. You can borrow books for free. Libraries also have story times and fun activities every week.'

Why does the author think libraries are great for children? Find two reasons.

steps: Ask: what is the author's point? Libraries are great places for children.
Look for reasons that support this point.
Reason 1: you can borrow books for free.
Reason 2: libraries have story times and fun activities every week.
Both reasons explain what makes libraries great for children.
solution.answer: The author thinks libraries are great for children because (1) you can borrow books for free, and (2) libraries offer story times and fun activities every week.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

'Eating vegetables helps you grow strong and healthy. Vegetables have vitamins that your body needs. They also give you energy to run and play.'

What does the author say is the reason you should eat vegetables?

steps: The author's point: eating vegetables helps you grow strong and healthy.
Reason 1: vegetables have vitamins your body needs.
Reason 2: they give you energy to run and play.
These reasons answer WHY vegetables help you.
solution.answer: The author says you should eat vegetables because they have vitamins your body needs and because they give you energy to run and play.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

'You should always wash your hands before eating. Washing removes germs that can make you sick. It also keeps dirt from getting in your food.'

What is the author's point? What reasons does the author give?

steps: The author's point: you should always wash your hands before eating.
I look for the word 'because' or any sentence that explains why.
Reason 1: washing removes germs that can make you sick.
Reason 2: it keeps dirt from getting in your food.
Both reasons support the point about washing hands.
solution.answer: The author's point is that you should always wash your hands before eating. The reasons are: (1) washing removes germs that can make you sick, and (2) it keeps dirt from getting in your food.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

'Helmets are important when you ride a bike. A helmet protects your head if you fall. Wearing a helmet can prevent serious injuries.'

What point does the author make about helmets? What reason is given?
items.hint: Find the sentence that says WHAT is important, then find the sentence that says WHY.

steps: Ask: what is the author's point? Helmets are important when you ride a bike.
Ask: why? Look for the reason.
Reason 1: a helmet protects your head if you fall.
Reason 2: wearing a helmet can prevent serious injuries.
Both reasons support the point about wearing helmets.
solution.answer: The author's point is that helmets are important when riding a bike. The reasons are: (1) a helmet protects your head if you fall, and (2) it can prevent serious injuries.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

'Cats are easy pets to care for. They clean themselves every day. Cats also do not need to be taken for walks.'

What is the author's point? What reasons support it?
items.hint: Look for the main idea sentence, then find the sentences that explain why the idea is true.

steps: The point: cats are easy pets to care for.
Reason 1: they clean themselves every day (you do not have to bathe them).
Reason 2: cats do not need to be taken for walks.
Both reasons explain what makes cats easy to care for.
solution.answer: The author's point is that cats are easy to care for. The reasons are: (1) they clean themselves, and (2) they do not need walks.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

'Children should spend time outside every day. Fresh air and sunlight help your body make vitamins. Playing outside also helps you sleep better at night.'

Why does the author think children should go outside? Name at least two reasons.
items.hint: Look for the sentences that start with reasons or include the words 'help' or 'also.'

steps: The point: children should spend time outside every day.
Reason 1: fresh air and sunlight help your body make vitamins.
Reason 2: playing outside helps you sleep better at night.
Both reasons answer WHY going outside is good for children.
solution.answer: The author gives two reasons: (1) fresh air and sunlight help your body make vitamins, and (2) playing outside helps you sleep better at night.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

'Bees are helpful insects. They make honey that people love to eat. Bees also help flowers grow by carrying pollen from one flower to another.'

What point does the author make about bees? What reasons support it?
items.hint: The point is stated in the first sentence. The reasons explain what helpful things bees do.

steps: The point: bees are helpful insects.
Reason 1: they make honey that people love to eat.
Reason 2: they help flowers grow by carrying pollen.
Both reasons explain specific ways bees are helpful.
solution.answer: The author's point is that bees are helpful insects. The reasons are: (1) they make honey for people to eat, and (2) they help flowers grow by carrying pollen.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

'Reading every day makes you smarter. Books teach you new words and new ideas. The more you read, the better you get at reading.

What does the author want you to believe? What two reasons does the author give?
items.hint: Find the sentence that makes the big claim, then look for the sentences that explain why that claim is true.

steps: The point: reading every day makes you smarter.
Ask: why does the author believe this?
Reason 1: books teach you new words and new ideas.
Reason 2: the more you read, the better you get at reading.
Both reasons support the claim that reading makes you smarter.
solution.answer: The author wants you to believe that reading every day makes you smarter. The two reasons are: (1) books teach new words and ideas, and (2) the more you read, the better you get at it.
